text: The Leelavati Award recognizes outstanding contributions to public outreach in mathematics. It is named after the 12th-century mathematical treatise "Lilavati," authored by the Indian mathematician Bhāskara II, also known as Bhaskara Achārya. This treatise, focused on arithmetic, algebra, and the decimal system, presents a series of arithmetic problems in verse form addressed to a person named Leelavati (possibly his daughter), followed by hints for solutions. The work served as the primary source of learning arithmetic and algebra in medieval India and was later translated into Persian, influencing mathematical education in West Asia. The Leelavati Prize was first awarded at the closing ceremony of the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM) 2010 in Hyderabad, India. It was established by the Executive Organising Committee (EOC) of the ICM with the approval of the IMU Executive Committee (EC) as a one-time international award for exceptional public outreach in mathematics. Due to its positive reception at the conference and in the mathematical press, the IMU decided to make the prize a recurring award given every four years, with the ceremony becoming a regular part of each ICM closing event. The prize is not intended to recognize mathematical research but rather outreach efforts in the broadest sense. It includes a cash prize of 1,000,000 Indian Rupees (equivalent to 14,000 US dollars) along with a citation, and has been sponsored by Infosys since 2014.
